ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; close the case and inform the rider that no refund is due.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider cancelled this on-demand RydeX trip herself at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance at 08:40:00, and the $6.61 cancellation fee is on record [F4][F7][NS-0]. NS-0 routes a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant booking through NS-4, and both advocates agree on that frame [F4][NS-0][NS-4].

NS-4 makes a rider cancellation free only within 3 minutes of matching; a cancellation after 3 minutes sustains the $6.61 fee [F4][NS-4]. The record shows 400 s, well beyond that window, so the fee stands and no refund is due [F4][F7][NS-4].

The rider's stated ground — "plans changed and the driver had not even arrived" — is contradicted by the system record: the driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:25 and stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 for 4 min 40 s [F1][F2][F3][NS-4]. NS-4 provides no relief for a driver who has not yet arrived, and here the driver had arrived; the rider's own message "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" confirms the cancellation was her change of mind, not a driver failure [F10][NS-4].

No separate refund trigger exists in the arrival/waiting record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m arrival radius), stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and the cancellation came 5 min 15 s after arrival [F5][F6][NS-1]. NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are therefore satisfied on the record and NS-2's refund condition is not engaged, so nothing turns on the no-show branch [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. The driver's post-trip statement that he was parked at the pickup is corroborated by the stationary GPS period and adds nothing either way [F3][F12][NS-1].

The fare record shows only the published $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge (1.0×) and no other add-on, so there is no unpublished charge to strike down under the fare rules [F7][F8][FARE-1]. Since no RD-1 route violation and no RD-2 refund arise in this no-show case, RD-6's flag condition is not met and no account flag is warranted [F5][F6][RD-6]. The parties' 90-day histories are background only and cannot decide the case [F16][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages and the driver's statement. Chat #1 is a neutral arrival notice and Chat #2 a polite apology with a cancellation notice; the driver's statement is a factual account of parking at the pickup [F9][F10][F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the complaint itself is a fare objection only [F11][F15][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The screen is therefore "none".

Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete with every message timestamped, the timeline and GPS records cover acceptance, arrival, the stationary period and the cancellation instant, and the fare record carries the fee [F4][F5][F6][F7][F11]. No record needed to apply NS-0/NS-4 is missing, so there is no evidence gap and no reason to escalate.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's excuse that 'the driver had not even arrived' fails against the system record: the driver was within 200 m from 08:41:25 and stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00; NS-4 gives no relief on that ground anyway [F1][F2][F3][NS-4].

The rider's own argument that a defect in the arrival record could refund the fee is not made out: the 'I'm Here' tap at 08:42:15 was 40 m from the pickup and 4 min 25 s of waiting followed; NS-1 is satisfied and NS-2 is not triggered [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's appeal to the parties' 90-day histories (driver 2 upheld no-shows, rider 0) is not a ground: profile facts cannot decide a case and RD-6 does not apply where no RD-1/RD-2 violation is found [F16][F17][RD-6].
The driver's non-arrival rebuttal is unnecessary to the outcome — the fee is sustained by NS-4 on the rider's own late cancellation alone, not by the arrival evidence [F4][F7][NS-4].

The driver's arrival/waiting compliance is corroborative only: NS-1/NS-2 are not the operative branch for a rider-cancelled instant booking, so these facts do not independently sustain the fee [F5][F6][NS-4].
The driver's point that the chat record is complete is accurate but neutral — it neither creates nor removes a refund ground under NS-4 [F9][F10][F11][NS-4].
